overrideWhichModelTierRunsFor: Override which model tier runs for specific kinds of agent work. Most users leave this on the workspace defaults — Economy for background tasks, Balanced for normal runs. wakeBudgetAlertLong: Budget alerts are quick acknowledgements — the agent reads the alert, decides whether to pause work or notify a human, and goes back to sleep. There is no heavy reasoning involved, so the cheapest tier is almost always enough.
wakeBudgetAlertRecommendation: Quick acknowledgement work → cheaper tier is enough.
wakeBudgetAlertShort: Agent is notified when a workspace or project budget is near its limit and may need to throttle or escalate.
wakeHeartbeatLong: Heartbeats keep an agent reactive: a quick scan of the inbox, open tasks, and budget alerts. They fire constantly in the background, so using a cheaper tier here can dramatically reduce your monthly spend without affecting the work that matters.
wakeHeartbeatShort: Periodic check-in your agent runs on a schedule (every few minutes) to see if anything new needs attention.
wakeRoutineTriggerLong: Routine triggers fire on a cron schedule that you control. The workload is predictable and rarely time-critical, so a cheaper tier is usually fine. Override per-agent if a specific routine needs the smarter model.
wakeRoutineTriggerRecommendation: Predictable workload → cheaper tier usually fine.
wakeRoutineTriggerShort: Scheduled jobs you have set up under Routines (e.g. "summarise PRs every Monday morning").
